headline: Maui County Salary Commission Meeting

meeting.summary: The Salary Commission heard a draft County of Maui salary study from MGT Consulting and voted to move its March meeting to March 28.
meeting.recap: The Salary Commission meeting was called to order at 9:05 a.m.[[0:00:44]] The commission heard a presentation of a draft County of Maui salary analysis by MGT Consulting.[[0:04:42]] The consultant said 21 of 25 comparable governments responded to the salary survey.[[0:14:07]] Option one sets pay ranges at the 50th percentile, the middle of the market.[[0:18:57]] The consultant said fire recovery was not specifically considered when setting the salary figures.[[0:39:05]] The consultant recommended a higher percentile, like the 65th, to help address cost of living and recovery.[[0:40:38]] The consultant said an updated final report could be ready within two weeks.[[1:03:25]] The acting chair proposed holding off on salary decisions until the report is final.[[1:05:31]] Staff said the Charter requires consulting the commissions that appoint department heads before a final decision.[[1:05:53]] The commission voted to move its March meeting from March 14 to March 28.[[1:13:00]] The chair has resigned; it is not yet clear whether from the chair role or the commission.[[1:14:05]] The vice chair will serve as acting chair until the term ends March 31, 2025.[[1:14:52]] The next agenda will include election of a chair and vice chair.[[1:21:29]]
meeting.next: Staff will work on sending letters asking the commissions that appoint department heads for feedback on salaries. A fifth letter will go to the East Maui Water Authority board, which appoints its director. Staff will follow up with the chair to learn the scope of her resignation. Staff will share an updated calendar showing the March meeting date change. A conference room on the sixth floor of the county building is reserved for March 28. A letter will ask the administration to attend the March 28 meeting. The final report will be posted with the meeting materials before the meeting. A letter may go to the council chair inviting thoughts on salary changes at the March 28 meeting.
